# Tickets

The tickets (`tickets/<DATE>_<SLUG>.md`, with their `.plan.md` and `.lock.md` siblings) live on the branch `agent-data`, never on a code branch. A `tickets` link at the repository root, if present, is a possibly stale copy: never write there.

Read and change them with the `tickets` command, always run by its full name: `npx @openagt/skill-tickets@0.1`. Every change it makes is one commit on the `agent-data` branch, pushed straight to the remote when the project shares its records. Never pass `--local` or `--force`: they are a person's.

Every command prints one JSON document; a refusal is `{"ok":false,"reason":…}` with why on stderr, exit 1; a wrong command line prints the usage on stderr, nothing on stdout, exit 2. Every `<file>` below is a ticket's filename (`2042-01-01_some-ticket.md`) or the `tickets/…` path a queue entry links to; `put` also takes the ticket's `.plan.md` and `meta.json`.

## Read

```
npx @openagt/skill-tickets@0.1 list                 every open ticket, as one JSON array; a row: file, title, summary, date,
                                                    planned, and when set priority, topics, issue, pr (set: the ticket is in
                                                    review), waiting (what it waits on), effort, uncertainty, outdated (the
                                                    plan says so), locked, lockedBy
npx @openagt/skill-tickets@0.1 show <file>          one ticket: its text, its plan, who holds it
npx @openagt/skill-tickets@0.1 meta                 when the tickets last caught up with the issue tracker:
                                                    {"lastImportedAt": <ISO 8601>}, or {} when no import was recorded
```

## Change

```
npx @openagt/skill-tickets@0.1 put <f
… 9473 characters cut …
d, its result, how it ended, and what it cost
```

## Before you plan or work a ticket, read its earlier runs

A ticket may have been worked before. Claiming it names who claimed it before you: a run's id, shaped like `2026-09-08T18-14-30-111Z`, read with `npx @openagt/skill-logs@0.1 show <id>`, or else a branch, read with `npx @openagt/skill-logs@0.1 --branch <name>`; no run on that branch means no record: read the branch itself. A `stopped` or `failed` run tells you what to avoid: read what its agent said before it ended. A `done` run with a `pr` means the work may already be there: read the pull request before doing it again.

## The card

```json
{
  "id": "2026-09-08T18-14-30-111Z",
  "startedAt": "2026-09-08T18:14:30.651Z",
  "endedAt": "2026-09-08T18:15:40.433Z",
  "status": "done",
  "intent": "what the agent was asked to do",
  "driver": "claude-code",
  "model": "opus",
  "branch": "agent-2026-09-08T18-14-30-111Z",
  "pr": { "number": 1765, "url": "https://example.com/org/repo/pull/1765" },
  "cost": 0.62
}
```

`status` is `running`, `done`, `stopped`, `failed` or `waiting` (ended on a question the agent asked, until it is answered). `cost` is in US dollars. Every field but `id`, `startedAt` and `status` is absent when unknown. The program that wrote the card may keep its own bookkeeping under one more key, `caller`; the command never prints it to you.

## The diary

One JSON object per line. Four kinds are the agent's, in the order they happened:

```
{"kind":"said","text":"…"}                       something the agent said
{"kind":"result","text":"…"}                     the agent's final answer for a turn
{"kind":"cost","usd":0.62}                       what a stretch of the run cost, in US dollars
{"kind":"ended","status":"failed","detail":"…"}  how the run ended; detail when it did not end well
```

Each line may also carry `at`, the time it was written, in the card's format.

Any other kind of line is the writing program's own; `show` leaves it out.

# Karten-Bounds, Kategorienavigation und klickbare Marker im Astro-MapShell umsetzen

## TLDR

Die bestehende Astro-/MapLibre-Karte soll auf `/map/`, `/map/overview/` und Kategorie-Seiten die jeweils passenden Orte als klickbare Marker zeigen und deren Bounds in den tatsächlich freien Kartenbereich einpassen. Kategorienavigation, lokalisierte Place-Links und die bestehende persistente MapShell sollen sauber integriert werden.

## Warum es wichtig ist

Das Ticket beschreibt einen konkreten agentischen Umsetzungsplan für die Karten-, Kategorie- und Navigationsansichten. Es gibt bisher keine Overview-Marker oder implementierte Kategorie-Routen; die Karte soll in allen Ansichten zur jeweiligen sichtbaren Ortsmenge passen.

## Geprüfter Ausgangsstand

- Astro `main`: [`f575c36`](https://github.com/richard-unterberg/astro-maplibre/commit/f575c363fb886dee82335c89340f32e2057a6df5).
- Designreferenz Vike `master`: [`ff66451`](https://github.com/richard-unterberg/maplibre-vike/commit/ff664513546d67d15b14c8936ad706fecbfad049).
- `lib/places.ts` lädt Overview und Details mit validiertem, gecachtem Build-Fetch. `getPlaces()` liefert IDs, Koordinaten, Kategorien, Detailzoom und übersetzt
… 5914 characters cut …
tiertem Seitenwrapper lesen, nicht aus alten Map-DOM-Attributen.
- Marker-Klick navigiert genau einmal zur serverseitig generierten lokalisierten Place-URL (z. B. über Astros `navigate()`); nur sichtbare Marker anklickbar, freie Karte ohne Navigation, Touch-taugliche Trefferfläche und Pointer-Cursor.
- Handler nutzen aktuelle Marker/URLs nach Kategorie- und Sprachwechsel.
- `load`/`style.load` und schnelle Navigation gegen verspätete alte Callbacks absichern.
- Event-Listener/Observer bei persistierter Navigation nicht duplizieren; bei tatsächlichem Austausch Karte und Ressourcen bereinigen.
- Listen bleiben echte tastaturbedienbare Place-Links.

## Prüfung und Abnahme

Gezielte Logiktests ergänzen/anpassen: Mehrfach-Kategorie-Filter/Deduplizierung; normale, einzelne/identische und leere Bounds; Padding ohne doppelten Header-/Panelversatz; Zustandswechsel und Detailbereinigung; Kategorien-Cache und Loader-Fehlerbehandlung. Bestehende `tests/placeFocus.test.mjs` anpassen, keine veraltete `height / 4`-Annahme.

Ausführen: `pnpm test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` und relevante Format-/Lint-/Knip-Prüfungen. Build-Ausgabe für Kategorie-/Place-Seiten beider Sprachen prüfen.

Browser-Smoke via Production-Preview auf Desktop und schmalem/mobilem Viewport: direkte Einstiege/Reload; Bounds in freier Fläche; korrekte Teilmenge/Navigation; Marker- und Sprachwechsel; Back/Forward; Theme-Wechsel; Resize/Panelhöhe; Listener-/Observer-Stabilität; keine Rezentrierungsschleife. Screenshots dokumentieren; falls kein Browser verfügbar, offenen visuellen Smoke benennen.

## Nicht Teil dieses Tickets

Kein React-Wechsel, keine neue State-/Animationsbibliothek, kein SSR-Adapter, kein Query-/Hash-Routing, keine zusätzlichen Laufzeit-Fetches und kein Clustering.

Technische Referenzen: [MapLibre FitBoundsOptions](https://maplibre.org/maplibre-gl-js/docs/API/type-aliases/FitBoundsOptions/), [Astro ClientRouter](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/view-transitions/).
